summary.headline: Anthem Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs 418 crore with 39.6% EBITDA margin; management guides to H2-weighted recovery, not a number.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 418 crore, with CRDMO at Rs 341 crore (81.5%) and Specialty Ingredients at Rs 78 crore (18.5%). EBITDA including other income was Rs 176 crore (39.6% margin), PAT Rs 120 crore (27.1% margin), and net cash stood at Rs 1,720 crore at June 30, 2026. Management attributed the soft quarter to customers deferring deliveries into Q2–Q4 rather than to demand weakness, and reiterated full-year growth in line with historical double-digit performance. Analysts pressed on the roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1; management pushed investors to judge the business on a YoY and full-year basis.

segments.name: CRDMO
segments.commentary: Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27 (81.5% of revenue); management says order book is about 60% of full-year plan after replenishment, with deliveries deferred to Q2–Q4. Analyst cited roughly 25% YoY decline in Q1.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Rs 78 crore in Q1 FY27 (18.5% of revenue); India-focused B2B business with rolling forecasts revised every 3 to 6 months. Management cited raw material and supply chain pressure from the war and expects decent growth by year-end.

guidance_outlook: Management says Q1 FY27 is the softest quarter of the year and expects sequential growth from Q2 onward, with recovery in Q2, Q3 and Q4.

Full-year FY27 growth expected in line with historical performance (double-digit over the last 10 years, per CFO); no specific percentage guided. Analyst's 20% growth figure was not confirmed by the company.
EBITDA and PAT margins expected to be broadly intact for FY27; management sees no margin challenge this year given the order book.
FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; capex elevated in FY28 due to Unit 4, then declining.
Tax rate expected to normalise to about 25% to 25.5% for the full year as Neo Anthem moves toward breakeven and profitability.
Semaglutide API commercial supply to domestic players expected after CDSCO approval, guided as likely within a quarter or two and in any case this year.
capex_capacity: Unit 1 utilisation about 78% in Q1 FY27 (about 74% at FY26 end), custom synthesis.
Unit 2 utilisation about 50% in Q1 on expanded custom synthesis capacity (about 130 kilolitres added); fermentation about 50% on 140 kilolitres. Unit 2 averaged about 65% in FY26.
Unit 3 (Neo Anthem) utilisation about 30% to 35% in Q1 FY27, up from about 15% in FY26; new projects including peptide synthesis and oncology manufacturing being moved in.

Unit 4: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 capex on about 30 acres (half of land used in Phase 1), adding about 365 kilolitres custom synthesis and 100 kilolitres fermentation, plus food and nutra plant. Groundbreaking last year; civil work nearly done; equipment orders starting; capex split about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28; commissioning by end FY28.
Management expects all units to approach optimum utilisation within about two years.
demand_pricing: Added one new Big Pharma customer in the quarter; agreement not yet signed, expected to contribute in later quarters of FY27. Management describes it as multi-dimensional (R&D, new projects, supply diversification).

One large biotech customer was acquired by a Big Pharma; management says impact is not material for the rest of FY27 and no meaningful discussions with the acquirer yet. The affected contract is a late-Phase 3 development contract, not commercial.

Four new molecules commercialised by customers last year; sizeable supplies expected only after a couple of years of market penetration. About 14 commercial molecules and 10 late-phase molecules, with 100+ early-stage programmes; commercialisation of late-phase molecules 18 to 24 months away. Two late-phase programmes are ADC-related.
Q1 deferrals attributed to customers rerouting stock between geographies and approval delays for growing molecules; management says confirmed orders remain in place.
Semaglutide: sampled almost all large domestic players; sales not yet started, pending CDSCO approval. Regulatory work started for other markets but none targeted yet.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation at Units 1, 2 and Neo Anthem, and US FDA or EU inspection timing for Unit 3?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 1 about 78%, Unit 2 about 50% (fermentation also about 50%), Unit 3 about 30% to 35%. Unit 3 growth is from new projects rather than shifting volume from existing units. Management did not give an inspection timeline in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on the next quarter and the split of the remaining 40% of the year's business across CRDMO, R&D and Specialty Ingredients?
qa_highlights.answer: The 60% order book figure applies to the whole business. Specialty Ingredients is month-to-month with rolling forecasts; CRDMO orders are placed in advance due to raw material procurement and manufacturing lead times. The remaining volume is expected from new customers and volume increases from existing ones.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year CRDMO growth after a weak Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said growth prospects remain intact and in line with historical double-digit growth, with recovery expected in Q2 to Q4 and margins mostly intact. CEO asked investors to judge on a YoY basis and not to treat any single quarter as a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Semaglutide commercial supply timing and inbound interest from domestic peers facing scale-up issues?
qa_highlights.answer: No commercial supply yet; awaiting CDSCO approval, expected this year. Management said the company is ready to scale, has sampled most large players, and was not responding to a peer's scale-up problem.

qa_highlights.question: Unit 4 capex, timeline and FY27 capex total?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,200 crore Phase 1 outlay, about 50:50 across FY27 and FY28, with commissioning by end FY28. FY27 capex target about Rs 700 crore; FY28 stays elevated before declining.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability over 3 to 5 years, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 60% order book and known cost base for FY27, and points to flow chemistry and biocatalysis as cost reducers. Material margin rose in Q1 despite lower revenue. Management expects some PAT dilution when new units start.

risks_watch: Lumpy CRDMO deliveries: Q1 soft due to customer deferrals; Q2 to Q4 must absorb the shortfall to hold full-year growth.
Semaglutide CDSCO approval timing; delay would push back the GLP-1 revenue ramp.
Acquisition of a large biotech customer by a Big Pharma; ramp-up timing and volume impact uncertain.
Unit 4 execution (Rs 1,200 crore, commissioning end FY28) and FY28 capex; PAT dilution as new units start.
Specialty Ingredients under raw material and supply pressure; management expects growth by year-end but gave no figure.
Neo Anthem (Unit 3) turning breakeven this year is needed to support the 25% tax rate assumption.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year growth and margins, but defensive on the Q1 top-line decline, repeatedly asking investors to judge on a YoY and full-year basis. Management gave no numeric growth guidance and was vague on the timing of the new Big Pharma contract and the biotech acquisition impact.
key_quotes: The underlying demand remains strong, with a higher concentration of scheduled deliveries in the latter half of the year.
We clearly see this Q1 as the softest quarter for the year.
Even after Q1, we have replenished the order book. Even right now, we stand with about 60% of the order book still being there.
So, please keep that in mind. Our business has to be looked at for the whole year holistically.
